explanations: Incorrect. Benchmark scores are not what a business audience needs, and they say nothing about this workflow's value.
Correct. Naming where human review remains, and why, is honest limitation-setting and is what makes the value claim credible.
Incorrect. Good instructions reduce error but do not eliminate it, so this claim is false and will damage trust later.
Correct. A measured pilot result is concrete evidence of value rather than an assertion stakeholders are asked to take on trust.
Incorrect. Promising that checking is no longer needed oversells the tool and sets the expectation that will break first.
